title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 136, the divided-power de Rham complex for the 1976 IHÉS talk). Grothendieck works with a cosimplicial (or functorial) family of commutative DG algebras with divided powers, (A_k)_n ≃ k{X_0,…,X_n}[dX_0,…,dX_n]/(Σ dX_i). Here k{…} is the divided-power polynomial algebra. This is a divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms on the n-simplex, presumably meant to model cohomology over arbitrary rings k, including Z and F_p. On this page he studies a morphism φ (a base change k→k', or an 'operation') of these structures. Its effect φ_* is determined by the images of generators: A'_1 is the image of a degree-1 coordinate, and B'_1 is a further generator (probably attached to dX or to the divided-power part). By compatibility with divided powers, B'_i = A'_1^{(i-1)} B'_1. He then lists successively stronger compatibility conditions and translates each into a normal form for A'_1 and B'_i.
(a) φ_* commutes with the divided powers of the B'_i.
(b) φ_* commutes with the exterior gradings.
(c) φ_* respects the 'coarse' increasing filtrations iff A'_1 = λ'X_0 and B'_i = Σ_{0≤j≤i-1} b'_{ij} X_0^{(j)}, with λ', b'_{ij} ∈ k'{T}.
(d) φ_* respects the 'fine' increasing filtration iff φ_0(k)⊂k', A'_1 = α'_0 X_0 with α'_0 ∈ k', and B'_i = Σ_{j+k≤i-1} α'_{ijk} X_0^{(j)} X_1^{(k)}.
He remarks that this last condition is empty when 2 is invertible in k', because then the B'_i vanish. So the extra B-data is a purely 2-primary phenomenon, presumably tied to divided powers or squares of odd-degree elements.
The fine filtration is made explicit. Fil_d consists of the forms Σ F dX_{i_0}∧…∧dX_{i_r} whose coefficients have 'degree' ≤ d−r. Equivalently, it is the smallest multiplicative increasing filtration with k⊂Fil_0, X_r and dX_r in Fil_1, Fil_i·Fil_j⊂Fil_{i+j}, and x∈Fil_d ⇒ x^{(i)}∈Fil_{di}. It is also the filtration attached to the total-degree grading in which X_r and dX_r both have degree 1. That grading is compatible with divided powers, makes (A_k)_n a graded module over a graded ring S, and has a differential of degree 0. A marginal NB contrasts the coarse and fine filtrations: the coarse one is presumably the least fine, generated by a graded subring. The aim seems to be pinning down which endomorphisms or functorialities of the dp de Rham model are 'rigid', i.e. linear in the coordinates.
errors: Indexing slip: dX_{i_0}∧…∧dX_{i_r} is an (r+1)-form. With dX of degree 1, the coefficient degree should then be ≤ d−r−1, not ≤ d−r, unless the wedge is meant to run over r factors.

Saying the graded structure has 'differential of degree 0' is consistent only because X_r and dX_r are given the same degree. This is fine, but it differs from the usual cohomological grading, which should be kept distinct.
Without the preceding pages the exact meaning of B'_1 cannot be confirmed (image of dX, or of an odd divided-power generator). The claim that the B'_i vanish when 2 is invertible fits the latter.

ideas.what: Cosimplicial divided-power polynomial de Rham algebra k{X_0..X_n}[dX_0..dX_n]/(ΣdX_i) as an integral/char-p analogue of Sullivan's forms
ideas.modern_name: divided-power (PD) polynomial de Rham forms on simplices; integral rational-homotopy models
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational case, 1977); integral/p-adic variants: Cenkl–Porter, Mandell (E∞), Toën (schematization revisited, 2020)
ideas.where_published: Only via the unpublished 1976 IHÉS talk; Pursuing Stacks mentions schematization themes

ideas.what: Characterization of the finest multiplicative, divided-power-compatible increasing filtration as the one associated with total degree (X and dX both of degree 1)
ideas.modern_name: weight/degree filtration on PD de Rham algebra

ideas.what: Classification of morphisms of the PD de Rham model compatible with PD, exterior grading, and filtrations, with extra 2-torsion data B'_i that vanishes when 2 is invertible
ideas.modern_name: automorphisms/endomorphisms of the cosimplicial PD de Rham algebra; 2-primary rigidity

missed.claim: Grothendieck classifies the endomorphisms or functorialities of the cosimplicial divided-power de Rham model of simplices. He finds that, after imposing filtration compatibility, there remains extra 2-primary freedom (the coefficients α'_{ijk} of B'_i) which disappears when 2 is invertible. An explicit rigidity/automorphism analysis of the integral PD Sullivan-type model, isolating a 2-torsion ambiguity, does not seem to be standard in the literature.
missed.quote: (cette condition est vide si 2 inversible dans k', dès lors les B'_i sont nuls!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic models of homotopy types (Mandell, Toën's schematization, binomial rings/Horel) wrestle with exactly how canonical PD-de Rham models are. A 2-primary non-uniqueness could relate to Steenrod-square-type phenomena.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step in Grothendieck's unpublished 1976 programme on a divided-power de Rham model for integral homotopy, which is itself little documented. The specific 2-primary observation is a modest but genuine unpublished detail. The mathematics on the page is otherwise routine filtration bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: Item labels: the first condition is 'a)', so 'B'_i = A_1'^{(i-1)} B'_1' (divided power of A'_1).
Item (b) likely reads 'commute aux graduations extérieures des B'_i ∀ i≥1'.
Item (c) parenthetical likely reads '(dont les termes ne sont pas des sous-k-modules)'; the final parenthetical is probably '(p. ex. minimum)', which is uncertain.
Margin NB plausibly reads: 'NB La filtration grossière est la filtration la moins fine … engendrée par le sous-anneau gradué … filtration finale'. This is uncertain.
